page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-lssd is a high-density compute instance powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors. It features 288 dedicated vCPUs across 144 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 1080 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core, and features a massive 504 MB L3 cache. Storage is heavily integrated, featuring 19031 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity distributed across 48 local drives.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core capabilities, with the stress-ng multi-core test and PassMark CPU suite scoring in the top 10% of all tested systems. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 1062.88 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 412.24 GB/sec for write operations. The instance also excels in data processing tasks, demonstrating top-tier performance in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and Redis SET operations, which reaches 407.31 million operations per second.

While multi-core and parallel processing metrics are highly competitive, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU benchmarks falling into the middle 50%. Additionally, despite strong prompt processing speeds for medium and large LLM models, text generation for smaller models is relatively weak, landing in the bottom 25%. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high resource density, combining massive compute power with extensive local NVMe storage, making it highly efficient for consolidated, IOPS-heavy workloads that can fully utilize its parallel architecture.

Given its hardware profile, the c4-standard-288-lssd is highly suited for large-scale database operations, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data compression pipelines. It is also well-suited for CPU-based LLM prompt processing and high-performance computing tasks that require substantial local storage and high memory bandwidth.

It delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and exceptional memory bandwidth, with read speeds exceeding 1000 GB/sec. While single-core performance and small-model LLM text generation are more moderate, the instance excels in parallel processing, database operations, and high-throughput data compression. This hardware profile makes it highly efficient for massive database deployments, software compilation, and IOPS-intensive workloads.
